answer_1.quote: We use a human-in-the-loop pipeline that combines LLM and expert input to generate stories and multiple-choice questions.

answer_2.quote: We also use multiple automatic measures of language complexity to compare concept definitions from Wikipedia and stories generated by different LLMs. These measures are ... (1) Legal Vocabulary List (LVL) occurrences, (2) Top 1000 most common words (Top1K), (3) Function words, (4) Sentence length, (5) Language model perplexity, (6) Flesch-Kincaid grade level.

answer_4.quote: We recruit human subjects with law education backgrounds on Prolific to evaluate the legal concepts and their corresponding stories generated by LLMs. ... We use a 5-item Likert scale ... for the generated stories: (1) Readability of Story (RoS), (2) Relevance, (3) Redundancy, (4) Cohesiveness, (5) Completeness, (6) Factuality, (7) Likeability, (8) Believability.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated stories on eight criteria using a 5-point Likert scale and rated questions overall on a 5-point scale while identifying errors.
